newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: East Timorese welcome U.S. criticism of Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: East Timorese welcome U.S. criticism of Indonesia.

text.p: The East Timor resistance on Friday welcomed U.S. criticism of Indonesia over human rights as a shift towards a tougher U.S. policy on Indonesia.
"I think it is long overdue," said Agio Pereira, a spokesman for the National Council for Maubere Resistance, the umbrella East Timor resistance group.
"The United States now needs to move to a clear-cut condemnation of the situation (in East Timor)," Pereira said.

Pereira said Indonesia was now on the Washington political agenda as a result of the controversy surrounding contributions from a wealthy Indonesia businessman to U.S. President Bill Clinton's 1996 re-election campaign.
"The White House was forced to focus more on Indonesia," Pereira told Reuters. "I think the right dynamics (for a tougher policy on Indonesia) are evolving in the United States..."
The U.S. State Department said in its annual human rights report released on Thursday: "The (Indonesian) government continued to commit serious human rights abuses."
The report said: "There were further instances of killings, disappearances, torture and excessive use of force by the military and insurgents" in East Timor.

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it a year later. Its occupation is not recognised by the United Nations which considers Portugal to be the administering authority.

East Timorese believe world opinion is shifting in favour of East Timor, citing the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize jointly awarded to East Timor Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo and East Timor resistance leader Jose Ramos Horta.
European Commission moves to support development aid in East Timor and the U.S. human rights report are also seen helping their cause.
"All these galvanising factors on East Timor are very powerful," said Pereira.
The Australian East Timor Assocation, which lobbies for East Timor independence, also welcomed the U.S. report as possibly representing a shift in U.S. opinion against Jakarta.
"I am encouraged that they are recognising this situation honestly," said the association's convener, Andrew McNaughton.
